# VideoFusion-Web

> Architecture and implementation notes for projecting live UAV video onto 3D reality-mesh scenes. Vue 3 + Cesium + EarthSDK3. Documentation only, no runnable source code.

Instead of showing drone footage in a corner monitor window and asking the
operator to mentally map it onto the 3D scene, this approach projects the video
frame onto the mesh surface itself, so imagery and terrain share one coordinate
space and occlusion, orientation, and coverage all stay consistent.

The hard part is not the API call. It is aligning camera extrinsics (position and
attitude), intrinsics (FOV and aspect ratio), and the model coordinate system. Any
mismatch shifts the entire projection. The second hard part is managing state
across multiple video streams: only one stream is projected at a time by design,
because concurrent projections visually interfere and multiply WebGL texture
memory.

## Documented architecture

- `src/components/CesiumViewer.vue` - the core: Cesium/EarthSDK3 init, ArcGIS
  imagery basemap, 3D Tiles loading, creation of drone entities and their
  `ESVideoFusion` projection objects, click-to-activate camera flyTo, screen-space
  connector synchronisation, and Home reset.
- `src/config/drones.js` - per-drone config: id, label, video URL, position,
  attitude, FOV, aspect ratio.
- `stream_server/start_stream.js` - Node Media Server for RTMP ingest plus an HTTP
  server on port 8088 serving HLS; ffmpeg slices a local MP4 into `index.m3u8` and
  `.ts` segments to emulate a live feed.
- `vite.config.js` - Vite plugins plus static asset copying for Cesium and
  EarthSDK.

## Notable conclusions

A single `<video>` element is reused; activation rebinds it to another
`ESVideoFusion` instance rather than recreating it, which avoids repeated decoder
initialisation stalls. Connector lines update inside the render loop, not on a
timer, otherwise they detach as soon as the camera moves. Home reset must clear
camera position, projection toggle, and selected-thumbnail state together.

## Known issues

Cesium Ion token was hardcoded in the original project and must be moved to an
environment variable before publishing. Canvas size is bounded by GPU texture
limits (4096x2160). Slice-based HLS has inherent multi-second latency; lower
latency requires WebRTC.
